message: I can hear cars far below and I keep imagining I'm not going to make it. What do I do first?
checked_steps: There is no safe place outside when thunderstorms are in the area.
Substantial buildings and hard-topped vehicles are safe options. Rain shelters, small sheds, and open vehicles are not safe.
A tent offers no protection from lightning.
Avoid open fields, the top of a hill or a ridge top.
Stay away from tall, isolated trees or other tall objects. If you are in a forest, stay near a lower stand of trees.
If you are in a group, spread out to avoid the current traveling between group members.
Stay away from water, wet items such as ropes, and metal objects such as fences and poles.
Wait 30 minutes after the last lightning or thunder before going back outside.
Stay calm and think through your situation.
If you're waiting for help, rest, save your energy and wait patiently.
Find shelter. Try to stay dry and cover all exposed skin.
If there's no shelter, build a lean-to or windbreak to block the wind.
If you have a wind- or waterproof jacket, wear it to keep out wind, rain and wet snow.
Wool or synthetic clothing is better than cotton. Cotton soaks up water and won't keep you warm when it's wet.
Keep your feet as dry as you can.
